Architecture Diagram

PartsUnlimited is a single ASP.NET web application with server-rendered storefront pages, a small Web API surface, and a shared Entity Framework data context. Business services and external integrations run in-process with the web application.

Data Storage & External Services

The web application uses a single SQL Server LocalDB connection for storefront and ASP.NET Identity data. Product lists and details are cached in-process. The recommendation component calls an Azure ML endpoint over HTTP and uses configuration for its model name and account key; social sign-in providers are also configured through application settings. No message broker or separate internal service was identified.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The application is a layered monolith with MVC and Web API presentation components sharing a single EF6 context.
  • Unity wires interfaces such as IPartsUnlimitedContext, query services, and external-service wrappers.
  • Recommendation failures handled as HttpRequestException return an empty recommendation list; no retry or circuit-breaker policy was identified.

DTOs & Contracts

The Web API serializes the Product and Raincheck domain entities directly; it does not use a gateway-level composition DTO. MVC requests use view models such as LoginViewModel, RegisterViewModel, and account-management models, while checkout accepts an Order. ShoppingCartRemoveViewModel and OrderCostSummary are response/presentation contracts. These are mutable classes rather than immutable records. Swashbuckle provides Swagger documentation, and Newtonsoft.Json is the JSON serialization library. No protobuf or GraphQL schema was found.

Communication Patterns

MVC controllers call application services and query classes synchronously or asynchronously in-process, and the EF6 context accesses the shared SQL Server database. The recommendation engine uses an outbound HTTP GET to Azure ML, with model and product identifiers in the request; an HttpRequestException is tracked and degrades to an empty recommendation list. No retry, timeout policy, circuit breaker, service discovery, load balancing, message broker, or cross-service response aggregation was found.

ASP.NET Identity/OWIN provides cookie authentication, two-factor flows, and external sign-in configuration. MVC controllers protect account-management, checkout, order, and administrative actions with authorization attributes; administrative controllers require the admin role. The two Web API controllers do not declare authorization attributes and are publicly callable at the application layer. The code does not enforce HTTPS for inbound requests; TLS behavior depends on the hosting configuration.

Core Business Workflows

PartsUnlimited supports an online parts storefront with product discovery, a session-associated shopping cart, order checkout, customer accounts, and administrative catalog management. Product recommendations are optionally enriched by an external recommendation service.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
ProductPartsUnlimitedWebsite / CatalogA part offered for sale with catalog, price, inventory, and recommendation dataBelongs to a Category; appears in order details, carts, and rainchecks
CategoryPartsUnlimitedWebsite / CatalogA grouping used to browse productsContains Products
CartItemPartsUnlimitedWebsite / ShoppingA product and quantity associated with a visitor's cartReferences Product; grouped by a cart/session identifier
OrderPartsUnlimitedWebsite / OrderingA customer's submitted purchase and delivery informationContains OrderDetails and is associated with a signed-in username
OrderDetailPartsUnlimitedWebsite / OrderingA product line captured when a cart is checked outReferences Order and Product
ApplicationUserPartsUnlimitedWebsite / IdentityA registered storefront or administrative accountIdentity data is used for sign-in and order ownership
RaincheckPartsUnlimitedWebsite / Store OperationsA store-issued record for a product not currently availableReferences Product and issuing Store
StorePartsUnlimitedWebsite / Store OperationsA store that issues rainchecksCan issue multiple Rainchecks

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
PartsUnlimitedWebsiteCatalog, Shopping, Ordering, Store Operations, and IdentityProduct, Category, CartItem, Order, OrderDetail, Raincheck, Store, ApplicationUserSQL Server database; optional Azure ML recommendation endpoint; configured social identity providers

All domain contexts are implemented within one application and share the same database/context. The Azure ML integration returns recommendation identifiers; it does not own application entities or perform cross-service data aggregation.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Add products to cart and check out

  1. A visitor selects a product; the cart service locates the visitor's cart using the session-associated cart identifier.
  2. The service increments an existing product line or adds a new cart item.
  3. A signed-in customer submits shipping/order details and a promo code at checkout.
  4. The checkout action accepts the configured FREE promo code case-insensitively; otherwise it redisplays the form.
  5. On acceptance, the application assigns the signed-in username and current date, creates an Order and OrderDetails from cart contents, computes the order total, empties the cart, and saves the changes.
  6. The completion action verifies that the requested order belongs to the signed-in username before displaying confirmation.

Workflow 2: Administer the product catalog

An administrator with the required role can list, create, edit, or remove products. The application validates product models before saving changes, clears affected cached product data, and broadcasts a product announcement through SignalR after a successful creation.

Workflow 3: Display product recommendations

When recommendations are enabled, the product detail view requests recommendation identifiers from the configured Azure ML endpoint. The application returns an empty recommendation list if the HTTP request fails or the response contains no recommendation set.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There are no internal service-to-service data flows. The only identified outbound business-data exchange is the recommendation request: the application sends configured model information and a product identifier to Azure ML, then uses the returned product identifiers for recommendations. If the HTTP call fails, the recommendation list is empty; product browsing remains available. No retries, circuit breaker, or local recommendation persistence was found.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Customer participant Checkout as "Checkout Controller" participant Cart as "Shopping Cart" participant Context as "Data Context" participant Database as "Application Database" Customer->>Checkout: Submit order details and promo code Checkout->>Checkout: Check promo code alt Promo code is accepted Checkout->>Context: Set customer identity and order date Checkout->>Context: Add Order Checkout->>Cart: Create order from current cart Cart->>Context: Add OrderDetail lines and clear cart Checkout->>Context: Save all changes Context->>Database: Persist order and cart updates Database-->>Context: Save result Context-->>Checkout: Order identifier Checkout-->>Customer: Redirect to completion Customer->>Checkout: Request completion Checkout->>Context: Verify order belongs to customer Checkout-->>Customer: Show completion or error else Promo code is rejected Checkout-->>Customer: Redisplay checkout form end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Checkout eligibility: The submitted promo code must match FREE without case sensitivity; the checkout action is restricted to authenticated users. Although the Order model has data-annotation constraints, the checkout action does not explicitly gate persistence on ModelState.IsValid.
  • Order ownership: Completion and order views scope customer access by the signed-in username; administrative order searches are separately role-protected.
  • Cart behavior: Adding an existing product increments its quantity. Removing a line decrements quantities above one and deletes the line at one. Checkout snapshots each product's current price into an order detail, computes an order total, and empties the cart.
  • Catalog validation: Product and order view models use data annotations for required values, lengths, ranges, and email/phone formats. The full persistence model and constraints are described in data-architecture.md.
  • Cost calculation: The shared shipping/tax calculator charges per item and applies a standard tax rate with a different rate for postal codes beginning with 98. The cart-removal response contains a separate displayed-total calculation, so its tax presentation may differ from the shared calculator.
  • Account rules: ASP.NET Identity enforces the configured password and user rules, supports two-factor flows, and protects administrative operations through role authorization.
  • Transactions and side effects: Order/cart changes are saved together through EF6 SaveChangesAsync; no distributed transaction or compensating workflow exists. Product creation emits a SignalR announcement after persistence. Checkout catches exceptions and redisplays the form rather than exposing the exception to the customer.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application targets .NET Framework 4.5.1 and uses older ASP.NET, OWIN, and JavaScript packages. The dependency scan found high-severity advisories for Newtonsoft.Json 10.0.3, Microsoft.AspNet.Identity.Owin 2.2.1, Microsoft.Owin 3.1.0, Microsoft.Owin.Security.Cookies 3.1.0, and jQuery.Validation 1.16.0; see the security findings for advisory details. dotnet list package --include-transitive could not evaluate this legacy Web Application project because the Visual Studio WebApplication MSBuild targets are unavailable on this Linux runner, so the dependency inventory is based on the direct declarations in packages.config.

  • packages.config is the package manifest; no lock file or central package version file was found.
  • Framework components are split across separate NuGet packages, including several OWIN and SignalR packages that share version lines.
  • The main project has no declared test-scoped packages.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The application persists its catalog, shopping, order, raincheck, and identity data in a shared SQL Server database through Entity Framework 6. The model is maintained in one web-application bounded context rather than through separate service-owned stores.

The EF6 context disables lazy loading. The codebase includes an initial migration and a database initializer that seeds catalog data. No Flyway, Liquibase, or separate schema migration service was found.

Caching Strategy

The application uses the process-local MemoryCache.Default; no distributed cache is configured. The home page caches top-selling and new-arrival product lists for 10 minutes, product details use a 10-minute sliding expiration, and selected latest-product data is cached for 10 minutes. Administrative create/edit/delete actions remove relevant entries. Cache state is local to each web process.

Data Ownership Boundaries

All domain and identity entities are owned by the single PartsUnlimitedWebsite application and share the same SQL Server database/context. There is no database-per-service or cross-service database access. Controllers and query services perform in-process LINQ-to-Entities queries; the Azure ML recommendation integration exchanges product identifiers over HTTP but does not share the application database. The application does not implement CQRS or an outbox pattern.
